title: Satan's Strength Broken
english: …others, Satan is called a strong city, and this is strong; for it is the custom of the God-inspired Scripture to liken the very strong to towers, walls, or cities, as we have previously said. As the blessed prophet Jeremiah said, God sets up a strong city and a bronze wall (Jeremiah 1:10). Once the Emmanuel was revealed to the world, the unholy crowd of opposing powers was lifted, and Satan was shaken from his depths; he has fallen in such a way that he is unable to rise or breathe again, and he does not expect to recover at any time.

Therefore, the poor people will bless you, and the cities of oppressed men will bless you. For you became a helper to every humble city, and a refuge to those who were despairing due to poverty, rescuing them from wicked men; a shelter for the thirsty, and a spirit for men of wrongdoing. They will bless you as people who are faint-hearted and thirsty; in Zion, from wicked men to whom you delivered us.

Israel was called to the knowledge of God through the pedagogy of the law, and was enriched by the things from God. For he was saved, and inherited the land of promise. The multitude of other nations, being immeasurable, is completely alien to spiritual goods; they are unprotected and without divine gifts, destitute and without shelter in a certain way, lacking the divine covering, lacking the wealth of virtue, and lacking anything worthy of praise, and is unworthy of wonder. But when Christ appeared, he freed them from the devil's greed and brought them to God, and they were enriched with the light of truth and the glory of the gospel; therefore, they send up joyful songs to God and the Father regarding the greatness of the evangelical polity.

O Lord, you made an ancient and true plan, summing up all things in Christ, and you enlightened those in darkness while overthrowing the rulers of this age; and just as certain cities are strong, the poor people will bless you, and all cities will glorify you. For you have become a helper to all, and a shelter to those afflicted by poverty regarding the ancestral goods, rescuing them from wicked men. For some were faint-hearted in Zion, like people thirsting, as we have previously said. And perhaps through these things the prophet shows us that there were those in Israel who thirsted for the Savior's presence, and for the Savior of all…

translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence with 'ἄλλων' (of others/among others).
The text ends mid-sentence with 'κα' (likely 'καὶ' - and).
The citation for Jeremiah is corrected to Jeremiah 1:10 based on the imagery of the strong city and bronze wall.
The phrase 'πνεῦμα ἀνθρώπων ἀδικουμένων' is translated as 'a spirit for men of wrongdoing' to reflect the context of the blessing/refuge.

title: Prayer for Peace with God
english: ...We call upon your name, Lord.
The holy prophets had a custom of making supplications for Israel, for they were God-loving and well-pleasing to God in their devotion.
Since Abraham's descendants have been destroyed from the root and are compelled to mourn the loss of their holy fathers, they see their own people being destroyed due to their unbelief in Christ.
The prophet Isaiah says, 'Lord our God, give us peace, for you have given us everything.' (Isaiah 26:12)
If you grant us peace, we will be filled with every good thing and have received the fullness of your gifts.

The kind of peace they are asking for must be considered, as they are either asking for Christ Himself, who is our peace, according to the Scriptures, or for something else that brings reconciliation with God.
Through Christ, we are reconciled to the Father, and this reconciliation is the foundation of our peace with God.
Those who have not yet believed and still have the stain of sin are separated from God and are rightly considered enemies, having a stiff neck and fighting against God's laws.
In contrast, those who are obedient and well-disposed, and are ready to do whatever pleases God, are also at peace with Him.
This peace comes from God's heavenly ambition and is a gift from Him.
Therefore, we pray that God would give us the ability to be at peace with Him, and with the abolition of sinful and detestable sin, may we be spiritually united to Him through the mediator Christ.
This is what has been correctly said through the voice of Paul: 'Having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.' (Romans 5:1)
Through Christ, we will become a possession and the inheritance of God.
It is wise to say, 'Lord, possess us, for we know no other but You, and we call upon Your name.'
To truly worship God, one must be single-minded and dedicated solely to Him, so that only He is known and revered, and no other false god is named or worshiped.
This is because God alone is the true God, existing by nature and truth.
The law given by Moses also teaches us, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only, and by His name.' (Deuteronomy 6:13)
However, those who are spiritually dead will not experience eternal life, and no physician can revive them.
You, Lord, have brought judgment upon the proud and taken away all their males.
May You add to their troubles, Lord, and bring evil upon all the proud of the earth who know the one true God, name His name, and count Him as their Lord, but refuse to submit to His will.
The prophet Isaiah's words are a plea for peace, and through faith in Christ, we can have peace with God.
translator_notes: The text begins and ends mid-sentence, indicated by the leading and trailing ellipses.
The phrase 'ἐπαριθμοῦντες αὐτῷ' was added to reflect the source text's ending, which emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and worshiping God alone.
baehrens: PG 70 In Is. book3-tomos1 rem mid

title: Removal of Iniquity
english: The altars will be reduced to fine dust, and the trees will not remain, for their idols will be cut down like a forest.
The prophet, having rebuked those who have acted impiously against the holy prophets, now speaks as if from the face of God, saying that the iniquity of Jacob will be removed.

This removal of iniquity is not like human judgment, for God's judgment is tempered with gentleness, and He overcomes human weaknesses, always conquering human petty-mindedness, and not always exacting punishment for earthly transgressions in equal measure.

The blessing promised to Abraham is the forgiveness of sins, which is the way of the blessing for those who have not done good, but have been forgiven, as God said to Abraham, 'I will bless you and multiply your seed' (Genesis 22:17).

If God had not blessed Abraham with the forgiveness of sins, his seed would not have been multiplied, for they would have been punished for their sins, but instead, the hypothesis of the blessing has been kept and passed to them, and they have received forgiveness.

The time will come when the faithful will be free from their transgressions, and this will happen when they wage war against the ancient error that has held them captive, and when altars and temples and the smoke of idols will be removed, and the temples built for lifeless idols will be consumed by fire.
As they cut down the trees and handmade objects that were once revered, they will be like a grove being cleared, and God will raise up those who have stumbled from Israel.
This is in line with the divine Paul's statement that when the fullness of the nations enters, then all Israel will be saved (Romans 11:25).

The complete destruction of temples, the removal of groves, and the addition of the destruction of statues will signify a change from the ancient error to the knowledge of truth, and the people will turn to the truth, abandoning their former idols and the works of their own hands.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the end.
The translation of the verb κατακόπτω as 'cut down' is literal, but other translations, such as 'destroyed', may also be possible.
The translation of the verb ἐκκόπτω as 'cut out' is literal, but other translations, such as 'removed', may also be possible.
